subject: Science
name: Science, Year 8
placeName: Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia, Tasmania, Australian Capital Territory and Northern Territory

points.title: Cells as the building blocks of life
points.brief: All living things are made of one or more cells, the smallest units that carry out the processes of life. Most can only be seen with a microscope.

points.title: Parts of an animal cell
points.brief: The nucleus controls the cell and holds its genetic material, the cell membrane controls what goes in and out, and cytoplasm is where most reactions happen.

points.title: Parts of a plant cell
points.brief: Plant cells also have a rigid cell wall for support, chloroplasts where photosynthesis happens, and a large vacuole that stores water and keeps the cell firm.

points.title: Using a light microscope
points.brief: Total magnification is the eyepiece lens times the objective lens. Focus with the lowest power first, then move to higher power for detail.

points.title: Specialised cells
points.brief: Cells have shapes suited to their jobs, such as long nerve cells that carry messages, red blood cells that carry oxygen and root hair cells that take in water.

points.title: From cells to organ systems
points.brief: Similar cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together in organ systems that keep the whole organism alive.

points.title: The digestive system
points.brief: The mouth, stomach and intestines break food down into small molecules, and the small intestine absorbs them into the blood.

points.title: The circulatory system
points.brief: The heart pumps blood through arteries, capillaries and veins, carrying oxygen and nutrients to cells and taking wastes away.

points.title: The respiratory system
points.brief: Air moves through the trachea and bronchi to the alveoli in the lungs, where oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out.

points.title: Transport systems in plants
points.brief: Xylem carries water and minerals up from the roots, and phloem carries sugars made in the leaves to the rest of the plant, much as blood vessels do in animals.

points.title: Layers of the Earth
points.brief: The Earth has a thin crust, a hot mantle that flows very slowly, and a metal core. The crust and top of the mantle form rigid plates.

points.title: What moves the plates
points.brief: Plates move a few centimetres a year, driven by convection in the mantle, ridge push at spreading ridges and slab pull where a plate sinks.

points.title: Divergent, convergent and transform boundaries
points.brief: Plates move apart at divergent boundaries, forming ridges and rift valleys; push together at convergent ones, forming mountains and trenches; and slide past each other at transform ones.

points.title: Earthquakes and volcanoes
points.brief: Most earthquakes and volcanoes happen along plate boundaries, such as the Pacific Ring of Fire, where plates grind, sink or pull apart.

points.title: Evidence for plate tectonics
points.brief: Matching coastlines, fossils and rocks across oceans, mapped sea-floor ridges such as Marie Tharp's, and magnetic stripes on the sea floor support the theory.

points.title: Igneous rocks
points.brief: Igneous rocks form when molten rock cools. Cooling slowly underground gives large crystals, as in granite; cooling fast at the surface gives small ones, as in basalt.

points.title: Sedimentary rocks
points.brief: Sedimentary rocks form when sediments are laid down in layers, buried and cemented over long times. They are where most fossils are found.

points.title: Metamorphic rocks
points.brief: Metamorphic rocks form when heat and pressure change existing rock without melting it, as limestone becomes marble.

points.title: The rock cycle
points.brief: Weathering, erosion, deposition, burial, heat, pressure, melting and uplift turn one type of rock into another, mostly over millions of years.

points.title: How rocks are used
points.brief: A rock's properties, which come from how it formed, decide its use, as First Nations Australians chose particular stones for grindstones and cutting tools.

points.title: Kinetic and potential energy
points.brief: Kinetic energy is energy of movement, including heat, sound and electricity. Potential energy is stored, such as gravitational, elastic and chemical energy.

points.title: Energy transfer and transformation
points.brief: Energy is transferred when it moves from one object to another, and transformed when it changes form, as chemical energy in a battery becomes electrical energy.

points.title: Energy flow diagrams
points.brief: A flow diagram shows the energy forms in a system in order, such as chemical to electrical to light and heat in a torch. Most changes also give off some heat that is not wanted.

points.title: Energy in a swinging or rolling system
points.brief: On a roller-coaster or a pendulum, gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy change back and forth as height and speed change.

points.title: Atoms and elements
points.brief: An element is made of only one type of atom and cannot be broken down chemically. Each has a one or two letter symbol, such as O for oxygen and Na for sodium.

points.title: Molecules and compounds
points.brief: A molecule is two or more atoms joined. A compound has two or more different elements chemically joined in fixed amounts, with properties unlike its elements.

points.title: Reading chemical formulas
points.brief: A formula shows the atoms in a substance. In H2O, the small 2 means two hydrogen atoms with one oxygen atom.

points.title: Telling elements, compounds and mixtures apart
points.brief: Particle diagrams and models show elements as one kind of atom, compounds as joined different atoms, and mixtures as separate substances together.

points.title: The periodic table begins
points.brief: Mendeleev arranged the known elements by mass and properties in 1869 and left gaps for elements not yet found. Metals sit on the left and non-metals on the right.

points.title: Physical changes
points.brief: In a physical change, such as melting or dissolving, no new substance forms and the change is usually easy to reverse.

points.title: Chemical changes
points.brief: In a chemical change, atoms rearrange to make new substances with new properties, and the change is usually hard to reverse.

points.title: Signs of a chemical reaction
points.brief: Gas bubbles, a new solid (precipitate), a colour change, light, or a temperature change suggest a chemical reaction has happened.

points.title: Reactions that release or take in heat
points.brief: Exothermic reactions release energy and warm their surroundings, such as burning. Endothermic reactions take in energy and cool them, such as an instant ice pack.

units.title: Science as a human endeavour and inquiry

points.title: Models of matter change over time
points.brief: Ideas about matter changed from Democritus's indivisible atoms to Dalton's atomic theory, as new experiments and instruments gave new evidence.

points.title: Science and decisions about resources
points.brief: Mining, or a plan to restore land after it, is weighed on its ethical, environmental, social and economic effects, including on Country.

points.title: Judging science in the media
points.brief: A science claim is more trustworthy when it names its source, shows its evidence and comes from experts, rather than from opinion or someone selling something.

points.title: Writing an aim and hypothesis
points.brief: An aim says what an investigation will find out. A good hypothesis links the independent and dependent variables and can be shown wrong.

points.title: Repeat trials and averages
points.brief: Repeating each trial and averaging the results reduces the effect of random errors and shows whether results are reproducible.

points.title: Risk assessment
points.brief: A risk assessment lists each hazard in a method, how likely and how serious harm is, and how to reduce it, such as safety glasses with acids.

points.title: Drawing a conclusion
points.brief: A conclusion answers the aim, says whether the data supports the hypothesis, and uses the results as evidence.
